'''Accel Schools''', styled '''ACCEL Schools''', is a for-profit [[education management organization]] that operates 77 [[charter school]]s and 15 [[online school]]s primarily in [[Ohio]]. Accel schools have operated on significantly lower budgets than other Cleveland schools.<ref name="pd180303">{{cite news|last1=O'Donnell|first1=Patrick|title=I Can charter schools turned over to Accel network run by former CEO of K12 Inc.| url=http://www.cleveland.com/metro/index.ssf/2017/03/i_can_charter_schools_turned_o.html |accessdate=24 January 2018|publisher=Cleveland Plain Dealer|date=March 3, 2017}}</ref>

==History==
Since 2014, it has taken over schools operated by I Can, [[Mosaica Education]], and White Hat Management.<ref name="pd160916">{{cite news|last1=O'Donnell|first1=Patrick|title=Some Cleveland schools have strong scores while district falters; new ACCEL charter chain shines (See rankings)|url=http://www.cleveland.com/metro/index.ssf/2016/09/some_cleveland_schools_have_st.html|accessdate=28 January 2018|publisher=Cleveland Plain Dealer|date=September 16, 2016}}</ref> According to the ''Wall Street Journal'' ACCEL Schools was launched in 2014. That year, the online school company K12 Inc. created Pansophic Learning, financed by Safanad Limited in Dubai. Accel was formed as Pansophic Learning's American-based charter school company.<ref name="0:2">https://www.washingtonpost.com/education/2022/01/14/charter-school-for-profit/</ref> In 2015, Accel became the largest charter operator in the state of Ohio, taking over 40 schools.<ref name="0:7">https://www.cleveland.com/news/2020/01/loophole-could-give-f-rated-charter-schools-millions-meant-for-better-schools.html</ref> In 2021, it had 50 schools and 23,000 students.<ref name="0:9">https://www.wsaz.com/2021/11/10/wsaz-investigates-charter-school-concerns/</ref>

As of 2022, Accel's CEO was Ron Packard. Accel managed 73 charter schools, either brick and mortar or online, in Washington, Arizona, California, Colorado, Indiana, Michigan, and Ohio,<ref name="0:2"/> and was branching into West Virginia.<ref name="0:3">https://www.wsaz.com/2021/11/12/charter-school-company-defends-its-poor-record-other-states/</ref> 64 of Accel's operated schools were in Ohio. Its real estate arm in 2022 was Global School Properties, which purchased properties and would rent them to Accel-operated schools.<ref name="0:2"/>  

Accel has been criticized for allowing its charter schools in impoverished neighborhoods to go into "unlimited debt," then paying interest to Accel for the loans.<ref name="0:2"/>

After issuing a notice of violation under the [[Toxic Substances Control Act]] to Accel in June 2024, later that month, the EPA ordered Accel Charter Schools Network to address lead paint and asbestos concerns at three of its schools in Ohio. This included restricting building access for testing.<ref name="0:1">https://www.epa.gov/newsreleases/epa-announces-order-requiring-accel-charter-schools-network-inspect-and-abate-asbestos</ref><ref name="0:4">https://www.wkbn.com/news/local-news/asbestos-lead-paint-violation-at-3-local-schools-epa-issues-violations/</ref> The schools later re-opened.<ref name="0:5">https://www.wkbn.com/news/local-news/schools-expected-to-start-on-time-after-asbestos-lead-detection/</ref>

In 2024, Accel operated 77 in-person public charter schools, and 15 online schools.<ref name="0:4"/> In December 2024, there were reports from former staff members that Cornerstone Academy, an Accel-owned school, had locked children in classrooms with a "nightlock" device. Accel confirmed the claims, calling the lock-ins a "training issue" that had not been authorized.<ref name="0:8">https://www.10tv.com/article/news/investigations/10-investigates/former-staff-members-cornerstone-academy-claims-kids-locked-in-classrooms/530-c1e17ecd-0e5f-4f98-8674-a347a4e8e40e</ref>

==Performance==
Across Ohio, Accel Schools has done well in rankings in Cleveland, however in Sandusky it isn't as high.<ref name="pd160916"/><ref name="sr170820"/>
